questions.scenario: You deploy an API to Azure Container Apps. The API must incur no compute charges when it receives no requests and must start automatically when requests arrive.
questions.question: Which configuration should you use?

options.text: Set the minimum replicas to 0 and use an HTTP scale rule
options.why: Correct. A minimum of 0 allows scale to zero, and an HTTP rule starts replicas when requests arrive.

options.text: Set the minimum replicas to 1 and use a CPU scale rule
options.why: A minimum of 1 keeps a replica running, and CPU rules cannot scale to zero.
A maximum of 0 would prevent the app from running at all.

options.text: Deploy the API to Azure Container Instances with restart policy Never
options.why: Container Instances does not start automatically when HTTP requests arrive.

questions.explanation: Scale to zero requires min replicas 0 and a rule that can wake the app, such as HTTP, TCP or an event scaler.

questions.question: You create a container app on the Consumption workload profile. Which CPU and memory combination is valid for each replica?

options.why: Correct. On Consumption, memory is 2 Gi for each vCPU.
The memory does not match the required ratio for 0.5 vCPU.
3 vCPU requires 6.0 Gi of memory.
The Consumption profile allows up to 4 vCPU per replica.

questions.explanation: Consumption allows 0.25 to 4 vCPU in steps of 0.25, with memory equal to twice the vCPU value in Gi.

questions.scenario: A container app has an HTTP scale rule of 50 concurrent requests per replica, a minimum of 0 replicas and a maximum of 6 replicas. The app receives 500 concurrent requests.
questions.question: How many replicas will run?

options.why: Correct. 500 divided by 50 is 10, but the maximum replicas setting caps the app at 6.
This ignores the maximum replicas setting.
The rule adds replicas as concurrent requests increase.
50 is the concurrency value per replica, not the replica count.

questions.explanation: Container Apps calculates the desired replicas from the rule and keeps the value between min and max replicas.

questions.question: You need to provision a container app by using the Azure portal. Which resource must exist or be created before the container app can run?

options.why: Correct. Every container app runs in a Container Apps environment.
App Service plans host App Service apps, not container apps.
Container Apps runs on a managed platform; you do not create an AKS cluster.
Container Apps does not require you to manage virtual machines.

questions.explanation: The create wizard lets you select an existing environment or create a new one, with a Log Analytics workspace for logs.

questions.question: Which two changes to a container app create a new revision? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.

options.why: Correct. The image is part of the revision template.

options.text: Changing the minimum and maximum replicas
options.why: Correct. Scale settings are part of the revision template.
Secrets are application-scope settings and do not create a revision.
Ingress is an application-scope setting and does not create a revision.

questions.explanation: Revision-scope changes include the container image, environment variables, resources and scale rules.
